title: Governor Hochul reports record affordable housing production under five-year plan
summary: Hochul announces 22,000 affordable homes created or preserved in FY 2025-26 and 81,000 to date toward the states five-year housing goal.
linkage_to_PET_TCAP: Signals continued emphasis on state-led production subsidies; supports argument that NYC should pivot its own subsidy dollars toward equity conversion rather than duplicating LIHTC-style production.
draft_legislation_update: In PET/TCAP findings section, add a clause noting that state production plans are on track while NYC subsidy reform must focus on ownership conversion and cross-system savings rather than new capital construction.

title: HUD proposes removal of disparate impact protection rules under Fair Housing Act
summary: HUD proposes to rescind regulations clarifying disparate impact liability, leaving enforcement to the courts and shortening public comment to 30 days.
linkage_to_PET_TCAP: Weakens administrative fair housing enforcement just as PET/TCAP relies on source-of-income and anti-displacement protections; increases litigation risk and the need for NYC and New York State to codify robust disparate impact standards in local law.
draft_legislation_update: Amend PET/TCAP bills to 1) incorporate explicit disparate-impact language in local fair housing and voucher anti-discrimination provisions, and 2) require HPD/HRA to apply a disparate-impact test to all PET/TCAP acquisitions and tenant-screening rules regardless of shifting federal guidance.

title: HUD advances rule weakening Fair Housing Act discriminatory effects standard
summary: Advocates warn that HUDs proposed rule eliminating discriminatory-effects regulations would make it harder to challenge systemic discrimination in housing and credit.
linkage_to_PET_TCAP: Confirms a coordinated federal rollback of disparate impact, increasing the importance of PET/TCAPs local enforcement architecture and New Yorks own Human Rights Law to protect voucher and equity-transfer participants.
draft_legislation_update: In PET/TCAP enforcement sections, add cross-reference to New York Executive Law Article 15 and mandate that HPD/HRA and the NYC Commission on Human Rights treat policies with unjustified disparate racial or disability impact as prohibited discrimination, independent of HUDs regulations.

title: Trump Administration issues executive orders on mortgage credit and housing deregulation
summary: Two executive orders framed as promoting mortgage access and removing regulatory barriers are criticized for eroding mortgage fairness protections and doing little to expand truly affordable housing.
linkage_to_PET_TCAP: Reinforces PET/TCAPs critique that deregulated private-credit expansion will not solve NYCs affordability crisis, and underscores the need for publicly governed credit-union finance and equity-transfer mechanisms insulated from federal rollbacks.
draft_legislation_update: Strengthen PET/TCAPs preference for mission-driven depository institutions and require all program-aligned mortgage or co-op share financing to comply with local fair-lending and anti-redlining standards even if federal CFPB/HUD rules are weakened.

title: New York budget deal set to roll back SEQRA barriers to new housing
summary: The FY 2026 budget includes changes to the State Environmental Quality Review Act to remove a major procedural barrier to housing production in certain areas.
linkage_to_PET_TCAP: Creates a more permissive backdrop for acquisition-rehab projects, but also heightens displacement and gentrification risk without explicit equity-transfer and anti-harassment provisions.
draft_legislation_update: Update PET/TCAPs ULURP and environmental-review sections to require equity-impact assessments and anti-displacement findings for any PET/TCAP project benefitting from streamlined SEQRA review, and to prioritize acquisitions that prevent speculative teardowns in newly upzoned areas.

title: Business and real estate lobby escalates attacks on Mamdani housing plan
summary: NYC real estate and business leaders denounce Mayor Mamdanis housing agenda as a 'house of cards,' warning of capital flight and stalled development.
linkage_to_PET_TCAP: Signals an organized opposition narrative that will also be deployed against PET/TCAP; provides an opportunity to position equity transfer as fiscally conservative, market-stabilizing, and pro-small-landlord compared with large speculative actors.
draft_legislation_update: Augment PET/TCAP legislative findings with explicit language on fiscal ROI, risk-sharing with credit unions, and protections for small owner-occupants to counter claims that equity transfer is anti-investment or destabilizing.

title: HUD rule allows faster evictions by aligning timelines to state law
summary: New HUD rule effective March 30, 2026 removes the federal 30-day notice or cure period for nonpayment in HUD-assisted housing, deferring to often shorter state and local timelines.
linkage_to_PET_TCAP: Raises eviction risk and churn among voucher and project-based tenants, reinforcing the case for local just-cause, right-to-cure, and equity-protection rules inside PET/TCAP buildings.
draft_legislation_update: Add a PET/TCAP 'tenant equity due process' section that guarantees minimum notice and opportunity-to-cure periods, bars equity forfeiture based solely on temporary arrears, and instructs HPD/HRA to maintain stronger local timelines even where HUD permits faster evictions.
